steps.title: Group and count the customer rows
steps.change: The five Karnataka customers form one group; Maharashtra forms another with just one customer. Customers is the only source because each customer row already carries State; grouping by that field needs no lookup.
steps.added_sql: SELECT State, COUNT(CustomerID) AS customer_count FROM Customers GROUP BY State ORDER BY State;
steps.sql: SELECT State, COUNT(CustomerID) AS customer_count FROM Customers GROUP BY State ORDER BY State;

steps.title: Filter whole groups and label the missing state
steps.change: The threshold is a condition on a whole group. Filtering missing states in WHERE would remove their rows before they can contribute to the Unknown group.
steps.added_sql:
select 
CASE
    WHEN State IS NOT NULL THEN State
    ELSE 'Unknown'
END AS State

, count(CustomerID) as customer_count
from Customers
group by state
having count(CustomerID)>=5
ORDER BY State ASC

steps.title: Apply the requested sort
steps.change: Delhi has the highest count. Karnataka and Unknown tie, so Karnataka comes first alphabetically. The preview happened to display the same order on these rows.
steps.added_sql: order by  count(CustomerID) desc, State asc
